what:
libsql migration spike result (2026-04-27, branch spike/libsql at .claude/worktrees/spike-libsql/): drop-in compatible after 1.5h spike. **750/750 tests pass.** TypeScript build clean (libsql ships better-sqlite3-compatible types literally — d.ts file even comments "Type definitions for better-sqlite3 7.6"). N-API ABI stability proven empirically: same `.node` binary loaded successfully under Node 22 (ABI 127) AND Node 18 (ABI 108), no rebuild — closes the bug class from memory #348.

**Required patches when migrating:**
1. **6 import sites** — `from 'better-sqlite3'` → `from 'libsql'`. Type signatures `Database.Database` work unchanged.
2. **bufferToVector polyfill** in `src/memory/embeddings.ts` — libsql QUIRK: `prepare().get()` returns BLOB as Buffer (compatible), but `prepare().all()` returns BLOB as ArrayBuffer. Patch: accept `Buffer | ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array`, branch on `instanceof ArrayBuffer`.
3. **Test cleanup helpers (10 test files)** — libsql doesn't auto-truncate `.db-wal`/`.db-shm` on `db.close()` like better-sqlite3 does. Tests using `fs.rmdirSync(dir)` after `db.close()` fail with ENOTEMPTY. Fix: `fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })`. Production has zero impact (we never delete .db files in production).
4. **package.json** — replace `better-sqlite3` dep with `libsql`, update esbuild `--external:better-sqlite3` flags (3 in build:dist scripts), update assertion in `src/__tests__/package.test.ts` (also fix incorrect comment that calls better-sqlite3 "an N-API addon" — it isn't).

**Other libsql quirks to know:**
- `_metadata: { duration }` field on every returned row from prepare().get()/all() — libsql adds query timing. Doesn't break our `as any` cast pattern but would break `toEqual()` on full row shapes. We don't use those.
- `pragma()` IS supported at runtime (libsql docs page at deepwiki/api.md says "currently unsupported" but that's stale — it works fine, returns same shape as better-sqlite3).
- FTS5 supported (verified by spike).
- libsql package ships platform-specific prebuilds via @libsql/[platform] sub-packages (npm pulls only the one matching host platform/arch).

**Perf delta vs better-sqlite3 (Node 22, real MemoryStore + recall path, after warm-up):**
- 500 memories: recall hot path ~2.55ms → ~2.95ms (+0.40ms / +16%). Sub-millisecond.
- 1000 memories: recall hot path ~4.14ms → ~5.24ms (+1.10ms / +27%). Still imperceptible vs hook latency budget (100s of ms).
- Search FTS5: 0.5-1ms range either way.
- Write path: ~0-0.5ms delta.
- Acceptable for 0.5.0 ship. better-sqlite3 IS the fastest SQLite driver in Node, so any swap costs perf — but absolute numbers stay in the imperceptible range.
why: The spike succeeded — we now know migration is viable AND know exactly what to patch. Storing the specific patches + quirks so the actual migration session (whenever it happens) doesn't re-discover the bufferToVector ArrayBuffer issue or the WAL/SHM cleanup issue under time pressure. Also captures empirical perf delta so future debates about "is this fast enough" have data instead of speculation. Complements #348 (root cause), #349 (just-works principle), #353 (N-API research framework) — this is the empirical proof point for those.
